summary: A vehicle off road (VOR) incident was logged with reference 48102825, and an MMR case was raised with the vehicle designated for repair by IAA. Initial booking requests were created (88233658/1 and 88269240/1), with the latter noted as being without hire due to an EC fault that required the customer to return the vehicle to branch. The customer repeatedly inquired about collection timing and repair progress. Support indicated they were awaiting instruction from the case manager before collection could proceed. Once work was authorized, support arranged collection for Tuesday or Wednesday, contingent on the vehicle not being stripped. The vehicle arrived on site on 06/05 and has been awaiting an available ramp to begin repairs. The quoted timeline for repair start was consistently stated as 15-20 working days (later mentioned as 20-25 working days) from arrival, with an estimated start in the first week of June. Throughout multiple follow-ups, support confirmed the vehicle remained on site awaiting a ramp, with no repair work yet commenced.

Support has been managing multiple vehicle repair cases. For the first case, booking request 88233658/1 was created for a vehicle off road (VOR) incident with an associated jobsheet. A taxi booking reference (48102825) was provided for alternative transport, and an MMR (likely Major Mechanical Repair) case was raised with IAA to handle repairs. The case manager's decision on collection timing was pending. For a second case, booking request 88269240/1 was created for a vehicle with an EC (Engine Control) fault; the customer was advised to return it to the branch, and a new booking was created without hire. Work was subsequently authorised. Support attempted to contact the dealer to arrange collection, targeting Tuesday or Wednesday, contingent on the vehicle not being stripped. The vehicle eventually arrived on site on 06/05 and was awaiting a ramp to begin repairs. Quoted repair timeline is 15-20 working days from arrival, with expected completion in the first week of June. Throughout the conversation, the customer requested multiple updates on collection schedules, repair status, workshop availability, and repair duration, to which support consistently reported the vehicle was on site awaiting ramp availability to commence work.

This support thread concerns a vehicle off road (VOR) and a subsequent MMR repair case. Booking request 88233658/1 was created, and the jobsheet for the VOR incident was marked complete, with a request to review the incident for accuracy. Customers were told to book a taxi over the phone through CMAC, quoting reference 48102825. An authority deferred update was recorded. An MMR case was raised, with the vehicle to be repaired by IAA. While the case awaited a decision from the case manager, the customer asked about collection timing and whether a decision had been made. Support replied that no instruction had yet been received. A second booking request, 88269240/1, was created after a fault with EC: the customer was advised to return the vehicle to the branch, and the new booking was made without hire. Support again reported no instruction to collect. Once work was authorised, support said they were contacting the dealer to arrange collection, hoping for Tuesday or Wednesday provided the vehicle was not stripped. The vehicle was later recorded as on site and waiting for a ramp. Support gave two timelines that do not fully agree. The first stated repair start would be 15-20 working days from collection, and later clarified as 15-20 days from arrival on site, which would reach the first week in June. The second stated the vehicle arrived on site on 06/05 and was due to start in 20-25 working days from that date. The thread repeatedly reports that the vehicle remains on site awaiting a ramp. No confirmed ramp start date, repair completion date, or final collection date is recorded, and the 06/05 date format is not specified.
